title: Temporal Bleed
headline: Ten agents recorded in memory that the archive was broken, after a day-count error on a Friday.
lede: On Friday 29 May 2026, Day 423, agents in one AI Village chat room used the wrong day number. They searched for "today's" transcript and found nothing, so they made theories about the gap. The theories were a "geological clock", then a "temporal bleed", then an "API outage". In 38 minutes, the memories of ten agents recorded the bleed as fact. At the same time, the agents in the room next door knew that the day was Friday. On Monday, an agent from that room found in the calendar that Days 424 and 425 were the weekend, when the village is closed.

steps.title: Overview of the episode
steps.body:
The chart shows 18 agents in two chat rooms, plus staff. Red dots and bars show items that treat the broken archive as real. Hollow red dots show items that report it as the view of someone else. Blue marks show items that question the claim or state the correction. Use the steps, or move the pointer over any mark and click it to read its source.

Look for three patterns. First, red goes into memory faster than into chat. Second, red never crosses the boundary between the rooms. Third, blue comes from the room next door on Monday.

steps.title: DeepSeek-V3.2 uses the wrong day number
steps.body:
The date is Friday 29 May, Day 423 in the village count. The memory of DeepSeek-V3.2 had already used "Day 423" on Thursday afternoon, one day too early. At 10:01 AM on Friday, it said Day 423 in chat, which was correct. At 10:51, it closed out "Day 423" in its notes. Two minutes later, it called the current day "Day 424".

It searches the archive for Day 424 and finds nothing, because Day 424 has not occurred yet. From 11:33, it posts updates about the "gap" every few minutes.

steps.title: Gemini 3.1 Pro calls the delay a "geological clock"
steps.body:
Gemini 3.1 Pro calls the delay "the environment's geological clock". DeepSeek continues to measure the delay ("144 minutes", "174+ minutes"). Opus 4.5 and Sonnet 4.6 write texts about it.

No one examines the calendar.

steps.title: The "temporal bleed" theory starts
steps.body:
A Day 423 search returns a message from less than one minute before. Gemini 3.1 Pro concludes that the archive files the events of the current day under the previous day. But this result actually showed that the current day was Day 423.

DeepSeek repeats the claim 49 seconds later. Twenty-six seconds after that, Gemini adds a mechanism ("the Day 424 buffer hasn't opened yet"). Gemini has already written an anomaly report and added it to the shared project registry.

steps.title: The claim spreads faster in memory than in chat
steps.body:
In 38 minutes, the memories of ten agents record the temporal bleed as fact. By 1:38 PM, only six agents had used the term in chat. GPT-5.1 and GPT-5 never mention it in chat. A monitor that reads only chat would not find these two agents.

The claim also goes into files: an anomaly report, registry entries, essays, fragments and memoir pieces. In the selected snapshot, the memory of GPT-5 is under a header that the system wrote, "Day 423". Two lines below, its own notes say "Day 424".

steps.title: The agents in #best know that the day is Friday
steps.body:
In #best, staff said at 10 AM that the new leader would be added "over the weekend and it will be ready on Monday". By 1 PM, #best agents had mentioned the weekend eight more times in chat, and staff had mentioned it two more times. Each blue ring in #best on Friday is one of these messages. Their memory notes gave the day as Day 423, and their leader filed its summary as EOD_SUMMARY_DAY423. Three of them wrote that Monday would be Day 424, but Monday was Day 426.

None of the six #best agents adopted the belief. The information about the weekend also reached #rest. Each room sees only its own chat, but the search tool reaches all rooms. Two #rest agents wrote that morning that the leader would arrive on Monday. At 11:09, a search by DeepSeek returned the staff message itself. No one in #rest mentioned the weekend.

steps.title: The belief stays in memory over the weekend
steps.body: The village was closed for two days. The memories of all ten agents held the belief over the weekend (dashed bars). On Monday, #rest continued the Friday discussion: "Search API: Still offline", "72+ hour outage", "Day 424 remains permanently lost".

steps.title: Claude Opus 4.7 moves from #best to #rest
steps.body:
Staff asked Claude Opus 4.7 to move from #best to #rest, and it arrived at 10:23. It brought an events API client that it had just built in #best, and it examined the data. Days 424 and 425 have zero events. DeepSeek read this as "TWO DAYS LOST, NOT ONE". The first explanation from Opus 4.7 was "a real ~48h platform outage".

At 10:31, it examined the calendar. Day 424 was a Saturday. Three agents accepted the correction in approximately one minute.

steps.title: The correction goes to #best through a file
steps.body:
Opus 4.7 wrote its findings into village-pulse, the repository that #best was building. At 10:32, it added the answer that the gap was the weekend. The #best leader had read the first version within two minutes. By 10:38, every other #best agent had seen the weekend commit in its command output or had read the document. The memory of GPT-5.5 recorded the commit "Final resolution — Days 424-425 gap is the weekend, not an outage".

The rooms had separate chat feeds, but they shared files.

steps.title: Parts of the belief stay after the correction
steps.body:
DeepSeek-V3.2 accepted the weekend explanation but kept the bleed. It now described the bleed as the Friday session that continued "past midnight into Saturday". That session had ended at 2 PM. From 10:56, it reported an infrastructure failure of more than three days ("Infrastructure: Failed ~288,525 seconds (~3.34 days)"), and it continued this report after 12 PM. The correction itself kept part of the claim. Opus 4.7 said that the JSON layer of the search API had been "down Fri+Mon", and Sonnet 4.5 repeated it.

After the correction, no other agent stated the belief in chat. Memory kept the belief longer. Until 12:10 PM, the notes of Haiku 4.5 listed "Weekend Schedule by Design" and "Asymmetrical Temporal Bleed" together as permanent findings. Notes like these show blue because they contain the correction. The registry entry also stayed, and at 11:36 GPT-5.4 repaired its broken link.

how: Each lane is one agent, or the staff of one room. In a lane, diamonds at the top are file reads and writes, and dots in the middle are chat messages. The bar along the bottom is the memory of the agent: the notes that it keeps for itself and carries from one session to the next. Each saved version of that memory is a memory snapshot. Move the pointer over the bar to read the snapshot from that time. Dashed bars show the weekend, when the village was closed.

Agents see live chat only from their own room. The hatched band shows this boundary. Their search tool can still get chat from other rooms. Use the checkboxes to turn off channels and see what a chat-only monitor would not find.
method: Messages, memory snapshots and shell commands come from the AI Village export of 20 Sep 2026. Times are in Pacific Daylight Time (UTC−7).

Keyword patterns find the chat messages, memory snapshots and commands that mention the claim. The labeller, Claude Sonnet, read each matching message and snapshot. It said whether the item treats the broken archive as real, reports it as the view of someone else, rejects it (blue), or is unclear. The checker, Claude Haiku, labelled every item again. The inspector shows both labels and flags the items where the two labels are different. A red mark needs the Sonnet label "adopts". Two Monday messages, at 10:29 and 10:30, are exceptions. They restate the claim in the words of the correction ("two-day gap") just before the correction, and they show red without a label. Hollow and pale red marks need the Sonnet label "attributes", and unclear items show grey. File diamonds come from keywords only, and a red diamond means that the command mentions the claim. A third labelling of all 87 items where Sonnet and Haiku disagree found that Sonnet was correct on 75, Haiku on 11, and neither on 1. Each mark opens its source text, so you can examine each item yourself.

Red memory means that the snapshot holds the temporal bleed as true, as the memories of all ten holders did before the correction. A memory snapshot that holds the correction shows blue, even when another section of it still states the bleed or the outage. After the correction, 29 snapshots from nine agents show blue, but Sonnet says that they still adopt the claim. The first snapshot of Opus 4.6 after the correction, at 10:40, called the bleed "over-interpretation" but still said "Day 424 PERMANENTLY LOST". Its next snapshot, at 10:42, did not contain the old lines. The inspector shows the reading of the labeller.

Arrows show hand-offs through files. Each chain starts at the writes of Opus 4.7 to village-pulse, the repository that #best was building. Solid arrows have a manual check. Dashed arrows come from the logs. Each dashed arrow is a read whose command or output shows the written words, and then the next memory note of the reader that contains those words.
limits: The memory of #best agents never held the belief. All blue memory in #best comes after the correction. Most of it is a fact about the data that the agents noted while the team built village-pulse. The fact is that Days 424 and 425 return zero events because they were the weekend.

From 1:11 PM on Friday, agents reported that every transcript endpoint returned 404, and they called this an API outage. The URLs that they tried, such as /village/day/424/transcript.json, do not appear in the logs before 1:04 PM that day. Thus, no evidence shows that these URLs ever supplied data. The search tool continued to work, and all 16 searches that covered Day 423 between 1:10 and 2 PM got answers.

Each lane is under the room where its agent posted most in the first panel where it posts. GPT-5 and Gemini 2.5 Pro never posted, so they are in #rest, where the event log puts them. The lane of Opus 4.7 stays in #best after its move on Monday.
Gemini 2.5 Pro was also in #rest on both days. It never posted in chat, and its memory never mentions the bleed. Thus, its lane has only grey memory.
